title: Make the in-process relay answer Full/Refused like the HTTP relay client
body:
## Summary
The co-hosted relay's in-process RelayApi (services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:289-315) maps every store error, Full included, to Unavailable, while the HTTP client (crates/table-relay/src/lib.rs:47-58) yields Full for 429 and Refused for other 4xx.

## Description
`impl table_relay::RelayApi for MemoryStore` turns Error::Full, Error::Missing and Error::Invalid into `table_relay::Error::Unavailable`, and its `poll` skips the `after > MAX_MESSAGES` check that `Client::poll` and the `/sync` route both apply. Two consumers read the difference: the HOUSE's `deliver` (services/house-seller/src/hosted.rs:739-747) logs a full relay as `error=unavailable`, and table-runtime's relay/house tests drive wallets against this MemoryStore, so the wallet's 'relay is full' path (crates/table-runtime/src/pairing_relay.rs:40) is never reached by them although the real HTTP relay produces it. Fixed: Full -> Full, Missing -> Refused(Other), Invalid -> Invalid, the cursor bound checked, and `deliver` maps relay Full to Error::Full so the operator line says `full`. Technique: rate-limiting/refusal-contract (one refusal vocabulary per contract).

## Flow
- fill the store to MAX_MAILBOXES with in-process creates
- the next in-process create returns Unavailable (today) instead of Full
- HOUSE deliver logs `house step=deliver ... error=unavailable` for a full store
- fix: map the errors in the RelayApi impl and in deliver; re-run table-runtime relay and house tests

## Expected impact
The operator's log distinguishes a full relay from an outage, and in-tree tests exercise the wallet's real capacity path. Could break table-runtime tests that expect Unavailable from this store (to be checked by the instrument run).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one error vocabulary for the mailbox contract on both transports
Before: 3 of 3 store errors collapse to Unavailable in-process; HTTP keeps them distinct
After: in-process create on a full store returns Full; deliver logs error=full
Method: simulation - walked the three error paths in both impls; the dependents (table-runtime) are outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:289-315 RelayApi for MemoryStore: .map_err(|_| table_relay::Error::Unavailable) x3
crates/table-relay/src/lib.rs answer_error: 429 => Full, 4xx => Refused
services/house-seller/src/hosted.rs:739-747 deliver: map_err(|_| Error::Unavailable)
instrument: rendezvous test: in-process RelayApi::create past MAX_MAILBOXES returns table_relay::Error::Full (red today: Unavailable); house-seller test with a capturing Log: deliver against a full store logs error=full; then cargo test -p table-runtime relay house_

title: Leave a trace when the public relay turns callers away for capacity
body:
## Summary
The standalone rendezvous relay writes no line and keeps no count when it refuses with 429 (store full, mailbox full, caller allowance used), so an operator cannot tell a full relay from an idle one.

## Description
MemoryStore returns Error::Full at six sites in services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs (create_by store cap and HTTP share/allowance, generation RNG, send count/byte caps) and the HTTP layer maps it to 429. The only operator output of the relay binary is `accept failed` (services/rendezvous/src/serve.rs:239). Per rate-limiting/limit-observability, a limiter with no readout has two visible states, silent and on fire: the allowance constants (CALLER_ALLOWANCE 128, HOUSE_RESERVE 64) were derived on paper and nothing would show if real traffic hits them. Fixed: a per-reason refusal counter (store/mailbox/allowance) with one rate-limited stderr line on each transition into refusing, fixed codes only, no caller address.

## Flow
- a caller creates CALLER_ALLOWANCE + 1 mailboxes
- the last create answers 429
- nothing is written anywhere
- fix: count refusals by reason, log the first per reason per window

## Expected impact
An operator sees capacity refusals in the host log and can retune the allowance from evidence. Risk: log volume if not rate-limited; the line must carry no address (PII).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - capacity refusals are observable
Before: 0 log lines and 0 counters across 6 Full sites
After: 1 rate-limited line per reason transition; counter readable by a test
Method: simulation - counted the sites; the sink and the rate limit do not exist yet to measure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:160-162 boxes.len() >= MAX_MAILBOXES => Full
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:173-175 http share / CALLER_ALLOWANCE => Full
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:215-220 mailbox and global byte caps => Full
services/rendezvous/src/serve.rs:239 eprintln!("accept failed: {e}") - the only log line
instrument: inject a Log sink into MemoryStore (as house-seller's Log trait); test: allowance exhausted -> exactly one 'relay refused reason=allowance' line over 10 refusals within the window, none containing an IP

title: 'Turned away' tile mixes a since-start count with all-time refused intents
body:
## Summary
The scoreboard's 'Turned away' tile (services/house-seller/src/scoreboard/scoreboard.js:350-353, 387-389) adds refused agent intents from every held deal, of any age, to refusals counted since the house started, under a caption that says 'since <start date>'.

## Description
`refusals(view)` = daily_limit + full + other (HouseRefusals, counted since `refusals.since`, the last restart: crates/table-proto/src/house_ledger.rs:412-421) + the sum of `refused_intents` over up to 500 deals regardless of when they were created. The sub-line then claims the whole number is 'since <day of refusals.since>'. refused_intents are also a different thing (the house's own agent stopped by its mandate inside a deal), not a table request turned away. After a restart the tile can show N turned away 'since today' when every one of them is older. Fixed: count only refusals.* in this tile (or filter deals by created_at >= since and label the intents separately).

## Flow
- house restarts at 09:00; a deal from yesterday holds 3 refused intents
- tile shows 3 'Turned away', caption 'since <today>'
- none of the 3 happened since today, and none was a turned-away request

## Expected impact
The public number means what its caption says. Risk: the 'No PayPal call' check (checkQuiet, scoreboard.js:209-219) reuses the same sum and must keep its meaning.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the tile's number matches its stated window and noun
Before: 1 of 2 summed sources outside the stated window (refused_intents)
After: 0; a page test with an old deal carrying refused_intents shows 0 in the tile
Method: simulation - walked the sum against the HouseRefusals doc; which semantics the owner wants is a copy decision
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
services/house-seller/src/scoreboard/scoreboard.js:350-353 r.daily_limit + r.full + r.other + deals.reduce(... d.refused_intents)
services/house-seller/src/scoreboard/scoreboard.js:389 ` · since ${day(view.refusals.since)...}`
crates/table-proto/src/house_ledger.rs:412-413 'counted since the house last started'
instrument: page test in witness.test.mjs: refusals {0,0,0, since T0+86400} and one deal created at T0 with refused_intents 3 -> t-refused reads '0' (red today: '3')

title: Count table requests the HOUSE queue turned away in its public refusals
body:
## Summary
A table request refused at the actor's door (queue full: 429) never reaches Seller::note_refusal, so the public `refusals` the scoreboard shows undercount exactly the overload case.

## Description
HouseHandle::ask (services/house-seller/src/hosted.rs:990-1004) returns Error::Full when the 4-slot TABLE_QUEUE is full, before the actor sees the request; only Seller::table calls note_refusal. HouseRefusals is documented as 'Table requests the house turned away before writing anything' (crates/table-proto/src/house_ledger.rs:412-413), and `full` reads 0 during a flood that answered 429 to every extra buyer. Fixed: the handle counts its own Full turn-aways in a shared atomic that the actor folds into refusals.full on publish.

## Flow
- 5 buyers POST /v1/house/tables while the actor is inside a 183 s PayPal step
- 4 queue, the 5th gets 429
- refusals.full stays 0; the 'Turned away' tile shows nothing

## Expected impact
The public record reports overload honestly. Risk: double-counting a request that is queued and then also refused by the actor (count only the queue-door 429).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every turned-away table request is counted
Before: 0 of the queue-door 429s counted (no path from ask() to note_refusal)
After: each queue-door 429 increments refusals.full once
Method: simulation - traced ask() and note_refusal; needs a shared counter to measure
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
services/house-seller/src/hosted.rs ask(): queue.try_send(...).map_err(Full => Error::Full, Closed => Unavailable)
services/house-seller/src/hosted.rs Seller::table(): note_refusal only here
crates/table-proto/src/house_ledger.rs:412-421 HouseRefusals doc and fields
instrument: house-seller unit test using handle_with_prefixes: fill the tables queue, one more table() -> Full; after the actor publishes, refusals.full == 1 (red today: 0)

title: Scoreboard's own 'shorter record' check diverges from the witness rule
body:
## Summary
checkHeads (services/house-seller/src/scoreboard/scoreboard.js:246-249) flags a shorter record only when the new head is also signed later (`cur.at > s.at`), while TableWitness.compareHeads and table_proto::compare_heads call any same-epoch shorter head 'shorter' unconditionally.

## Description
witness.js says its rules 'mirror table_proto::compare_heads case for case' (witness.js:4-5), and witnessVerdict uses them for a visitor's file. The page's own stored-look check re-implements the shorter/rewritten cases with an extra time guard. A same-epoch head with fewer rows and an `at` not after the stored look (a clock set back on a restored disk, or a look saved by a later visit) falls through: no prefix is asked (no stored look is shorter than cur), verdict stays null and the check reads ok 'The same record this browser saw'. Fixed: use W.compareHeads for every stored look in the epoch, and decide in a test what the time guard was for.

## Flow
- browser stored a look rows=14 at T+2000
- house serves rows=10 signed at T+1000 (clock moved back)
- check renders ok instead of bad 'shorter'

## Expected impact
The page and the visitor-file check agree on what 'removed' means. Risk: if the guard existed to tolerate a look from a later concurrent tab, removing it could show a false 'shorter' (the instrument must cover that case).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one shorter/rewritten rule on the page
Before: 2 implementations of the rule; the page's misses a shorter head with at <= stored at
After: 1 implementation; a page test with the case above renders bad
Method: simulation - walked the case through checkHeads and compareHeads; the guard's intent is unrecorded
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
services/house-seller/src/scoreboard/scoreboard.js:247 if (cur.rows < s.rows && cur.at > s.at) return bad(...)
services/house-seller/src/scoreboard/witness.js:68-71 compareHeads: later.rows < kept.rows => 'shorter' (no time guard)
crates/table-proto/src/house_ledger.rs:285-287 same, no time guard
instrument: page test in witness.test.mjs: stored look {rows 14, at T0+2000}, served head rows 10 at T0+1000 -> heads check state 'bad' (red today: 'ok')

title: Domain-tag the HOUSE table answer and release-pin signatures
body:
## Summary
Two signatures in the HOUSE trust path carry no domain tag: the agent's signature over a HouseResponse (crates/table-proto/src/house.rs:97-99, 130-136) and the owner's release-pin signature over the raw 32-byte mandate commitment (house.rs:38-41), which is the same message form as a HELLO's owner_sig_over_commitment (envelope.rs:233-235).

## Description
Every newer signature in this crate is domain-separated: heads and prefixes (house_ledger.rs:156-159, 217-225), owner accepts ('table.owner.accept.v1', envelope.rs:107-114), pairing JWS headers (pairing.rs:31). The agent key also signs JWS inputs, closed mandates, pairing identities and raw commitments; the owner key signs mandates, wallet envelopes and raw commitments. No live collision was found (a HouseResponse's canonical bytes are a 3-element array no other signed form produces, and pins are compiled in, never accepted off the wire), so this is defence in depth per signed-artifacts/canonical-hashing. Adding a tag changes bytes that shipped wallets and the hosted HOUSE verify: a versioned wire change with readers outside this tree.

## Flow
- agent key signs canonical (seller, mandate, table) with no tag
- owner key signs the raw commitment, identical to a HELLO commitment signature
- a future signed form that encodes to the same bytes would verify as the other

## Expected impact
Closes cross-protocol signature reuse by construction. Breaks every wallet build and HOUSE release that verifies the untagged form unless both forms are accepted for a transition window.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every signature in the HOUSE path is domain-separated
Before: 2 of 6 signature kinds in house.rs/house_ledger.rs/envelope.rs untagged
After: 0 of 6 (with a v2 form and a transition)
Method: simulation - enumerated the signed forms per key; a wire change cannot be verified against out-of-tree readers here
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
crates/table-proto/src/house.rs:97-99 canonical_bytes(&(&self.seller, &self.mandate, &self.table)) - no tag
crates/table-proto/src/house.rs:38-41 verify_strict(&self.mandate_commitment.0, owner_signature)
crates/table-proto/src/envelope.rs:233-235 owner.verify_strict(&mandate_commitment.0, &sig) (HELLO)
crates/table-proto/src/house_ledger.rs:156-159 HOUSE_HEAD_DOMAIN / HOUSE_PREFIX_DOMAIN (tagged)
instrument: n/a - external contract (the hosted HOUSE and shipped wallets verify these bytes); needs a decision on a v2 form and a transition window

title: Sweep expired mailboxes on reads too
body:
## Summary
Reads leave expired mailboxes in memory until the next create/send.

## Description
read/batch filter expired boxes (services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:238, 397) but only create/send call Inner::sweep (lib.rs:156, 206). Every capacity decision is made inside create/send, after a sweep, so a held-but-expired box never changes an answer.

## Flow
- a box expires; only reads follow
- the next create/send sweeps before checking the caps

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - capacity answers after expiry
Before: 0 wrong capacity answers (expired_mailbox_releases_its_bytes and the allowance-expiry test pass)
After: 0
Method: probe - read both cap paths against the existing expiry tests
Result: not-better
Gate: none
evidence:
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:156 inner.sweep(...) in create_by
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:206 inner.sweep(...) in send
